extracted.intended_audience: senior corporate public relations executives and communications professionals (press release writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the Arthur W. Page Society's seven principles of corporate public relations to the writing and evaluation of press releases, emphasizing truth, stakeholder awareness, long-term thinking, and professional tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The public should know what's happening. Provide an ethically accurate picture of the enterprise's character, values, ideals and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core Page Principle: press releases must convey accurate, verifiable information about the organization rather than misleading impressions or omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove It with Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Public perception of an enterprise is determined 90% by what it does and 10% by what it says.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should be supported by substantive organizational behavior and real change; avoid announcing initiatives that are not backed by action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to Stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand what the public wants and needs. Keep top decision-makers and other employees informed about public reaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should demonstrate awareness of stakeholder concerns and reflect input or understanding of affected publics; ensure leadership is informed of public response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage for Tomorrow
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate public reaction and eliminate practices that create difficulties. Generate goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate press release content for future reputational effects; avoid short-term tactics that harm long-term trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct Public Relations as if the Whole Enterprise Depends on It
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate relations is a management function. No corporate strategy should be implemented without considering its impact on the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat press release strategy as integral to overall corporate strategy; coordinate messaging with business decisions and management objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realize an Enterprise's True Character is Expressed by Its People
rubrics_metrics.description: The strongest opinions—good or bad—about a company are shaped by the words and deeds of its employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes, spokespeople, and employee-related content in press releases reflect authentic behavior and values of staff; vet for consistency with organizational conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain Calm, Patient and Good-Humored
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay the groundwork for PR miracles with consistent and reasoned attention to information and contacts. When a crisis arises, remember cool heads communicate best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a composed, professional tone in releases (especially during crises); avoid reactive, emotional, or inflammatory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifiable facts, no spin, no exaggeration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press releases should contain only information that can be substantiated; avoid agenda-driven phrasing, unsupported superlatives, or deceptive framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backed by action (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announces real change, not just claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that any announced initiatives, policies, or commitments are implemented or funded; do not issue releases that promise changes without follow-through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder-aware (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipates how multiple publics will react.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess impacts on customers, employees, investors, regulators, and communities; craft messaging that addresses likely questions and concerns from those groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term oriented (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Doesn't sacrifice future trust for short-term gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tactics that may produce immediate media attention but erode credibility or stakeholder relationships over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aligned with overall enterprise strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the release advances organizational goals and is coordinated with broader corporate communications and business plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentic (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reflects what the company actually is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone, content, and claims should be consistent with the company's demonstrated behavior, culture, and values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composed (press-release application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional tone, even in crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain measured, factual, and respectful language; avoid sensationalism, sarcasm, or emotional appeals that undermine credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: All claims verifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: All claims verifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every factual assertion in a press release should be checkable against reliable evidence or documentation; avoid untestable or vague claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: All quotes accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: All quotes accurate (people actually said this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not fabricate, alter, or misattribute quotations; ensure spokespeople approve attributed statements where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: All data sources cited
rubrics_metrics.description: All data sources cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting statistics or research, cite the source, methodology, and limitations so journalists and stakeholders can verify context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about uncertainties, scope limits, and what is not yet known; disclose caveats that materially affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest revealed
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest revealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose relevant relationships, financial interests, or other potential biases that could affect credibility of the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder impact considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholder impact considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and state how the announcement affects customers, employees, communities, and other stakeholders; address mitigation where negative impacts exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term consequences accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term consequences accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge and accept responsibility for downstream effects of the announcement; avoid framing that evades accountability for future outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone professional and measured
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone professional and measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use restrained, respectful language; prioritize clarity and accuracy over persuasion or hype.
